title: Choose the visual world
question: Roll de50035e assigned Time-Impact Sheet (candidate 7 of 7). Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Time-Impact Sheet
options.lineage: the time-scaled baseline programme and as-planned-vs-as-built delay window — the drafting language these same people already use to argue an EOT
options.thesis: The register is a time-scaled sheet, not a sortable table. Every letter is pinned to the contract calendar, so an unanswered stretch is a visible empty span rather than a number you have to trust. Refuses the category default: the slate data-table with a left sidebar, filter chips and a blue accent.
options.viewport: A drawing title block across the top states the package, the period covered, and completeness as fact — 'NH-XX PKG-3 · 14 Mar 2023 – 09 Aug 2026 · 10 of 10 ingested · 0 unread'. Beneath it, the sheet: a fixed left index column carrying Sr. No. / date / letter ref. in the Excel register's own column grammar, and to its right a time axis running the full contract period. Each letter is a tick on that axis — outward above the centreline, inward below, exactly as a plan sits above a profile. Position carries direction; no colour does. The 47-day gap in the middle of 2024 is empty sheet, and you can see it before you can read it.
options.risk: A time axis can imply schedule analysis the register does not actually perform — it charts correspondence, not float. And if the ticks bunch, the axis smears at 1366×768. Both are real; both are fixable with a strict collision rule, and neither is deniable.

raised.raise: Exactly one struck emphasis on screen at a time. The selected letter is full ink and crisp; every other letter stays present but at reduced ink. Nothing else competes for emphasis — no second highlight, no hover glow, no active-state accent.
The scanned page is never boxed in a card. Evidence runs full-bleed and the chrome retreats to corner-pinned readouts at the safe-area margins, so the paper is never a thumbnail inside our furniture.
Where colour appears it owns a whole region at full height — a full-height band down a row — never a scattered dot, pill or chip.
One monumental typographic moment is permitted per screen. The elapsed-span readout is set at display scale, not table scale — the only place this dense sheet raises its voice.

options.label: Despatch Register
options.lineage: the bound government inward/outward despatch register and the file noting sheet — treasury ruling, Sr. No. columns, numbered paras, red-ink noting in the margin
options.thesis: The direct ancestor of the Excel file they keep today, done properly. Ruled columns that never move, a running serial number nothing can reorder, and margin noting where the machine's extraction annotates the clerk's row.
options.viewport: One continuous ruled register, serial numbers running down the left edge, extraction annotations set in the margin like a noting sheet.
options.risk: This is where most runs land once they know the incumbent is an Excel register — and it is the safest thing to show a contracts manager. Its strength and its ceiling are the same fact: it looks like what they already have, so it proves familiarity rather than capability.

options.label: Teletext Service
options.lineage: broadcast teletext magazines — 40×24 character cells, three-digit page addressing, the fixed broadcast eight
options.thesis: Every letter carries a three-digit address you key directly. No search field, no filter UI — you type the number and you are there. The rigid character lattice does the density work a table normally fakes.
options.viewport: An index page, letters as numbered rows in a strict cell grid.
options.case: Holds product clarity — direct addressing maps exactly onto letter reference numbers, and a fixed cell lattice is honest density. Loses audience identification: the black ground breaks light-mode-only and the meeting-room projector, and a bitmap face cannot set Devanagari.
options.risk: Reads as retro novelty the moment the grid slips, which is fatal in front of a tribunal.

options.label: Cyclorama Dawn
options.lineage: stage lighting cyclorama — horizon bands from night through cobalt and rose to white day, lighting-plot stencil caps, a scrubbable cue timeline
options.thesis: The dispute as a cue sheet. Named, deep-linkable states you scrub between, every transition inspectable, colour never the sole signal.
options.viewport: The chronology as a scrubbable cue timeline, phases stacked as horizon bands.
options.case: Holds product clarity outright — named, deep-linkable, text-equivalent states with 'colour is never the sole signal' as a system rule is close to purpose-built for an evidentiary chronology. Loses audience identification: the depthless black cyc ground breaks light-mode-only, and dawn-to-day as a metaphor for a contractual dispute is decoration a tribunal would not forgive.
options.risk: Atmosphere reads as interpretation, and interpretation is the one thing this tool has no standing to offer.

options.label: Struck Cathode Gauze
options.lineage: nixie decade counter behind bronze anode gauze
options.case: Loses both axes. Dark ground and glowing orange break light-mode-only and the projector; 'no rules, boxes or dividers anywhere' is a defect, not a feature, in a dense evidentiary table.
options.kept: Exactly one struck emphasis at a time — everything else present but subordinate.

options.label: Viewfinder Bracket HUD
options.lineage: camcorder OSD — corner focus brackets, zebra stripes, tape counter
options.case: Loses both axes. Blend-mode chrome composited over a scanned Authority Engineer letter destroys the legibility of the evidence, and the reference is a pop-culture toy to a 55-year-old contracts manager.
options.kept: Evidence always full-bleed beneath; chrome pinned to the safe-area corners, never occupying the centre.

options.label: Studio Dumbar Identity
options.lineage: modular Dutch identity — saturated blocks snapped over photography
options.case: Loses both axes. Cyan-magenta-yellow bars over a government letterhead is precisely the clash the constraints forbid, and 'looking like a startup product' is a disqualifier the author named directly.
options.kept: Colour owns whole regions at full height rather than scattering as accents.

options.label: Alphabet Storm
options.lineage: letters condensing into weather and reshaping the ground
options.case: Loses both axes, catastrophically. Language as reversible physical consequence is the opposite of a register whose entire value is that nothing moves and nothing is reinterpreted.
options.kept: One monumental typographic moment is permitted, even in a dense tool.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The legal-tech docket table, executed impeccably. White ground, slate ink, one blue accent, left sidebar of packages, filter chips above a sortable table, a right drawer for the document.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar, filter row, sortable table, detail drawer — the arrangement the visitor expects, at full craft.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every document-review platform they have already been pitched, and its drawer pattern collides directly with your 'no progressive disclosure' rule.
